To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amylopositive and amylonegativedatasets provided in the paper are not balanced and the training set is not representative for the testing set.
the method of extending datasets proposed by the Pafig authors is wrong and the incorrect data can lead to a false classification.
the method of dataset selection used by the authors of the Pafig tool leads to incorrect classification and the results of this method cannot be used for training models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of correct dataset selection for computational studies.
the question of the reliability of the results obtained by computational methods.

the importance of the selection of training and testing datasets in computational biology and bioinformatics, as the selection of datasets may have a strong effect on the results of the classification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Pafig does NOT provide correct classification with respect to amyloidogenic hexapeptides.
the method is not applicable for the purpose of the study and should be used only as a tool for generating new hypotheses.
the method is not suitable for amyloid propensity prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method for extending amyloid hexapeptidic datasets is incorrect and should not be used for any other purposes.
the authors of Pafig have not followed the standard rules of data science.
Pafig is not a useful tool for amyloid classification of peptides and proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is not possible to extend the amyloid dataset with the help of other datasets, because the datasets of different amyloid proteins are too diverse and there are no common patterns that could be used to extend one dataset with another.
the use of a wrong dataset can result in a falsely correct classification.

the selection of the experimental data for training and validation of the models should be done with extreme care, as the results of classification can be strongly influenced by the selection of the data.
